question: When the same scientific help can save lives or cause harm, who should decide what an AI answers?
reflection: Openly reporting how tools are misused can teach all of us to build better guards, not just faster tools.

sources.subject: Claude was asked to make a virus worse
DeepSeek 552B beats its own Pro model, then kills it

one_line: AI misuse moved from theory to case files, as a major lab reportedly detailed real attempts to turn its model toward weapons, hacking and surveillance.

top_stories.title: Anthropic details how people tried to misuse Claude
top_stories.what: Anthropic published a report on blocked misuse across seven areas, from cyber attacks and scams to biology, and says it banned accounts and alerted authorities.
top_stories.why: Telling harmful intent from honest research is partly a behavioural question, and labs will need evidence on how real users phrase risky requests.

top_stories.title: AI-written requests swamp public services
top_stories.what: A study of 84 public-service systems in 11 jurisdictions reportedly found complaints and applications rising sharply since generative AI became common.
top_stories.why: Government agencies face more, longer and more polished requests, and need ways to triage them without shutting out genuine citizens.

top_stories.title: DeepSeek's cheaper model replaces its flagship
top_stories.what: DeepSeek released V4.1-Flash, a large mixture-of-experts model that it says beats its own Pro model on speed, cost and quality, so Pro is being retired.
top_stories.why: Falling prices for strong open models make local, self-hosted AI more realistic for organisations with strict data rules.

saudi_lens.text: As Saudi platforms such as national complaint and licensing portals grow, the reported surge of AI-drafted requests abroad is an early signal for how service queues here may change.

idea.title: AI-assisted citizen requests audit
idea.pitch: Measure how the length, tone and volume of citizen requests change when people draft them with AI, and design fair triage rules.
idea.first_step: Ask one service team for an anonymised sample of requests from two years and compare their length and structure.

idea_kids.title: Helper or harm? Sorting game
idea_kids.pitch: Children sort picture cards of tools, like a knife or a medicine, into good uses and careful uses, then invent a rule for each.
idea_kids.first_step: Draw ten simple tool cards and write one helpful use and one careful-use rule on the back of each.

terms.definition: Scientific work that can be used for good, like vaccines, or for harm, like weapons.
A model design that only switches on a small part of its parameters for each task, which saves cost.
When an AI system helps build a stronger successor, which then speeds up the next round.

concepts.summary: Labs publish case reports on how people tried to use models for harm and how they were stopped.
Public agencies adapt to citizens using AI to write requests and complaints.
Cheaper models match or beat earlier premium ones.
